messages:
incident-bot: PAGER ALERT — high-rate auth success events from a single client_id across regions (count=3.2k, 5m) :rotating_light:
pagerbot: Paging oncall: @emma (primary) — please ack and triage.
emma: acked. jumping in. pulling recent auth logs now.
emma: quick check — are these internal service tokens or user sessions?
mike: looks like service-to-service tokens. seeing repeated JWTs with same kid.
tara: tagging security. suspicious: repeated valid tokens used from multiple IPs within minutes. could be token replay or key compromise.
carla: adding network — I see spikes from two cloud providers — ASN mismatch vs normal.
emma: initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle client_id, 2) temp deny-list suspicious IPs, 3) rotate the signing key for that client_id. anyone object?
mike: go for throttle + IP block now. I'll put a temporary rule in edge WAF.
carla: applying IP block: `iptables` style rule on edge cluster done — block list pushed to all regions.
pagebot: NOTE: Customer impact may be 502s if client_id uses graceful fallback. Monitor error rate.
emma: starting key rotation prep. Tara, we need to know if downstream systems trust the rotated kid immediately.
tara: security note — rotate keys with a short overlap window: publish new public key (kid=b:new) and keep old accepted for 5m. we'll revoke old after verification.
legal: please confirm if any customer data was exfiltrated or logs leaked — we need initial incident classification.
emma: no evidence of data download so far — only auth successes. logs show mostly token validation events.
mike: running `jq` on auth stream, found ~250 tokens re-used across accounts. attaching sample: ```
{"ts":"2026-03-20T10:02:13Z","client_id":"svc-analytics","kid":"a:1234","ip":"52.45.10.3","uid":"svc-123"}
```
tara: that's consistent with a compromised signing key or accidental key copy. priority: rotate keystore entry and force short TTL for issued tokens.
carla: coord with infra — how many services need new keys? looks like 3 service principals are signed by that key.
emma: I'll coordinate a canary rotation in staging then push to prod. plan: 1) publish new kid public key 2) update token issuer to sign with new kid 3) notify consumers to fetch JWKS 4) revoke old kid after 5m overlap 5) rotate service credentials for any affected SAs.
mike: I'll prepare the rollout script. using `rcli keystore rotate --kid old --new kid_b --overlap 300`
emma: running rotation now on a single region (us-west-2) as canary. monitor auth-errors and latency.
carla: observed 0.8% auth error spike during rollout window — expected. watch for customer-facing regressions.
pagerbot: Customer impact flag: none yet, minor auth retries observed for background jobs. Ops: open support ticket template to keep buyer-facing teams informed.
legal: keep me posted on any sign of logs leaking to external buckets. start a preservation hold on relevant logs.
tara: initiated keystore rotation and short TTL policy. also spinning up enhanced audit for all token issuances.
emma: canary looks good. promoting rotation to all regions in 2m.
mike: global rotate started. pushing new JWKS to CDN and invalidating local caches.
carla: WAF blocks holding steady, no new IPs after initial block.
emma: rotation complete. revoking old kid in 5m. collecting post-rotation metrics.
pagerbot: Post-rotation checks: token replay count dropped 98% after revoke.
tara: creating incident ticket (SEV-2) with timeline, IOCs, and mitigation steps. recommending full credential sweep for svc principals and mandatory rotation for affected customers if any tenant tokens issued.
legal: agreed on SEV-2 classification. prepping customer comms hold for potential notice.
emma: follow-ups: 1) run full keystore audit, 2) rotate affected service account keys, 3) search for potential leakage paths (CI logs, S3 uploads), 4) update runbook with overlap best-practices.
mike: I'll push automated key-rotate playbook to repo and tag for oncall run next week. PR incoming.
carla: leaving network blocks in place for 24h, will re-evaluate.
tara: closing live mitigation. continuing forensic analysis. I'll share IOCs in #sec-intel when ready.
emma: thanks team — great response. will update status page if any customer impact changes. :white_check_mark:
